baseline: Your tests pass on the real Thermostat

variants.name: cold-room-switches-off
variants.label: a cold room switches the heater off instead of on
variants.hint: Make the sensor report a cold room and expect the heater to be turned ON.

variants.name: warm-room-never-switches-off
variants.label: a warm room never turns a heating heater off
variants.hint: Heat first (a cold reading), then report a warm room, and expect turn_off().

variants.name: turns-on-every-time
variants.label: a cold room turns the heater on again at every update
variants.hint: Check the room several times in a row: how many times may turn_on() be called?

variants.name: reads-the-sensor-twice
variants.label: update() reads the sensor twice
variants.hint: An EXPECT_CALL with Times(1) (or a WillOnce) limits the number of reads.

variants.name: edge-of-the-band-switches
variants.label: a reading exactly at target - hysteresis already turns the heater on
variants.hint: The dead band is closed: exactly 19.0 (target 20, hysteresis 1) is still inside it. Test the boundary.

variants.name: failure-keeps-the-heater-on
variants.label: a failing sensor leaves a heating heater on
variants.hint: When the sensor throws, the heater must be turned off for safety. Use Throw(...) as the action.

variants.name: failure-is-reported-as-success
variants.label: update() returns true after a sensor failure
variants.hint: What does update() return when the sensor throws?

variants.name: not-a-number-is-trusted
variants.label: a NaN reading is treated as a normal reading
variants.hint: A sensor can return NaN. The documentation says what must happen then.

variants.name: switches-off-when-already-off
variants.label: a warm room calls turn_off() even when the heater is already off
variants.hint: With a StrictMock, any call you did not expect is a failure: check a warm room with the heater OFF.
